column1:
When and why do you use the
Pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo?
column2:
A completed event under a present-tense trigger. Take any frame from the present subjunctive and put the subordinate event in the past.
  • Emotion or doubt about something already done — me alegro de que hayas venido.
  • Uncertainty about whether it happened — no creo que lo haya visto.
  • Future completion under a trigger — cuando hayas terminado, avísame.

column1:
Tricks and tips for the
Pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo
column2:
• Purely compositional — nothing new if the present subjunctive and the participles are solid.
  • Spelling watch: haya (subj. of haber), halla (he finds), aya (nanny), allá (over there) are near-homophones. Only the first is a verb form of haber.
